plants.name: Sarracenia purpurea
plants.tip: The hardiest of the genus and fine outdoors all year. The pitchers hold their own rainwater, so never tip them out.
plants.colour: Squat green pitchers veined and flushed maroon

plants.name: Sarracenia purpurea subsp. venosa
plants.tip: Squatter and hairier than the northern form. Full sun all day, or the red veining never colours up.
plants.colour: Low broad pitchers, green to deep maroon with dense red veins

plants.name: Sarracenia purpurea f. heterophylla
plants.tip: No red pigment at all, so judge the light by pitcher size rather than colour. Rainwater only, tray topped up.
plants.colour: Entirely yellow-green, with green flowers and no veining

plants.name: Sarracenia flava
plants.tip: Tall trumpets that want a metre of headroom and full sun. Cut the spent pitchers down in late winter, not autumn.
plants.colour: Yellow-green trumpets with a red throat blotch and flared lid

plants.name: Sarracenia flava var. rubricorpora
plants.tip: The red tube only develops under direct sun. In part shade it comes up green and stays that way all season.
plants.colour: Deep red tube with a contrasting yellow-green lid

plants.name: Sarracenia flava var. atropurpurea
plants.tip: The darkest flava. It needs a full day of sun and a cold dormancy, or the colour thins and the plant weakens.
plants.colour: Wholly deep red, tube and lid alike

plants.name: Sarracenia flava var. ornata
plants.tip: The veining is heaviest on late-summer pitchers. Stand it in rainwater and never put it in ordinary compost.
plants.colour: Green tube with heavy dark red veining over lid and throat

plants.name: Sarracenia flava var. rugelii
plants.tip: One of the largest and easiest. Give it a deep, wide pot, as the rhizome runs sideways a little each year.
plants.colour: Plain yellow-green with a single dark red throat blotch

plants.name: Sarracenia flava var. maxima
plants.tip: Without red pigment it looks the same in sun or shade. Give it full sun anyway or the pitchers grow weak and flop.
plants.colour: Uniformly yellow-green, without any red marking

plants.name: Sarracenia flava var. cuprea
plants.tip: The copper lid deepens through summer. Keep the pot standing in rainwater and never feed the compost.
plants.colour: Green tube topped with a coppery bronze lid

plants.name: Sarracenia leucophylla
plants.tip: The autumn flush is the showy one. Leave those pitchers standing until late winter rather than trimming them off.
plants.colour: Green tube topped with white panels netted in red veins

plants.name: Sarracenia leucophylla 'Tarnok'
plants.tip: The mutant flower sets no seed, so divide the rhizome in early spring if you want more of it.
plants.colour: White-topped pitchers with red veins; flowers a tuft of sepals

plants.name: Sarracenia alata
plants.tip: Understated and very hardy. It wants full sun and a genuinely cold winter rest, outdoors wherever you can manage it.
plants.colour: Slim pale yellow-green trumpets with faint red veining

plants.name: Sarracenia alata 'Black Tube'
plants.tip: The near-black colour needs hours of direct sun. In a shaded greenhouse corner it comes up dull green instead.
plants.colour: Near-black maroon tubes with a dark lid

plants.name: Sarracenia minor
plants.tip: The hood curls over the mouth so rain never fills the trap. Water the tray, never the pitcher.
plants.colour: Green hooded pitchers with white windows and a red-flushed back

plants.name: Sarracenia minor var. okefenokeensis
plants.tip: The giant form, and slow for its first few years. Deep pot, full sun, and patience rather than feeding.
plants.colour: Tall hooded pitchers, green with white windows and red veins

plants.name: Sarracenia oreophila
plants.tip: It stops making pitchers by midsummer and puts out flat leaves instead. That is normal, not a failure.
plants.colour: Broad yellow-green trumpets with a faint red throat

plants.name: Sarracenia rubra
plants.tip: Small and clump-forming, and the flowers genuinely smell sweet. Full sun, rainwater, and no feed at all.
plants.colour: Slender coppery-green pitchers with fine red veins

plants.name: Sarracenia rubra subsp. gulfensis
plants.tip: The tallest of the rubra group. Divide it every third spring or the clump crowds itself into small pitchers.
plants.colour: Tall slim pitchers, green ageing to bronze with red veins

plants.name: Sarracenia psittacina
plants.tip: It lies flat and traps like a lobster pot. Keep it wetter than the rest, and let it sit flooded over winter.
plants.colour: Ground-hugging rosette of red-veined pitchers with white windows

plants.name: Sarracenia × catesbaei
plants.tip: A vigorous old hybrid that forgives more than either parent. Rainwater and full sun still decide whether it thrives.
plants.colour: Broad green pitchers with red veining and a flared lid

plants.name: Sarracenia × moorei
plants.tip: Tall enough that wind snaps the pitchers. Give it a sheltered sunny spot and cut back only in late winter.
plants.colour: Tall trumpets with white upper panels and red veining

plants.name: Sarracenia × mitchelliana
plants.tip: Squatter than the trumpet hybrids and very hardy. Stand it in rainwater all summer and let it freeze in winter.
plants.colour: Stout white-topped pitchers flushed maroon

plants.name: Sarracenia × excellens
plants.tip: The hood keeps rain out, so judge watering by the tray rather than the trap. Full sun brings up the veining.
plants.colour: Hooded white-windowed pitchers with dark red veins

plants.name: Sarracenia × popei
plants.tip: Mid-sized and reliable. Peat and sand only, as any compost with fertiliser in it kills the roots within a season.
plants.colour: Yellow-green trumpets with red throat veining

plants.name: Sarracenia × areolata
plants.tip: Slow to bulk up but long-lived. Full sun through summer and three cold months of rest each winter.
plants.colour: Slim pitchers with white patches and fine red netting

plants.name: Sarracenia × swaniana
plants.tip: Compact enough for a windowsill bog pot, though it still needs a cold winter spent outdoors.
plants.colour: Short hooded pitchers, green with white windows and red veins

plants.name: Sarracenia × chelsonii
plants.tip: One of the reddest hybrids, and the colour depends entirely on direct sun rather than on anything you feed it.
plants.colour: Squat deep red pitchers with heavy veining

plants.name: Sarracenia × formosa
plants.tip: Half-lying like its psittacina parent. Keep it very wet and it spreads into a low mat over a few years.
plants.colour: Small decumbent pitchers with white windows and red veins

plants.name: Sarracenia × wrigleyana
plants.tip: Often sold as a shop plant in ordinary compost. Repot into peat and sand as soon as you get it home.
plants.colour: Squat white-topped pitchers with strong red veining

plants.name: Sarracenia × courtii
plants.tip: Tolerates standing water better than most of the genus. Never let the tray run dry in summer.
plants.colour: Low half-upright pitchers, red-veined with white flecking

plants.name: Sarracenia × readii
plants.tip: Mid-height and slow. Divide only once the pot is full, as it sulks for a year if cut up too young.
plants.colour: Slim pitchers with white upper panels and red veining

plants.name: Sarracenia × harperi
plants.tip: The partial hood keeps the traps dry, so water from the tray with rainwater and leave the pitchers alone.
plants.colour: Green trumpets with a partly hooded lid and red throat

plants.name: Sarracenia × exornata
plants.tip: Squat and very hardy. A cold wet winter outdoors suits it far better than any indoor windowsill.
plants.colour: Broad pitchers, green flushed maroon with red veins

plants.name: Sarracenia 'Judith Hindle'
plants.tip: The usual garden-centre Sarracenia. It reddens properly only after a full day of direct sun, not a bright windowsill.
plants.colour: Squat pitchers with white throats and dense red veining

plants.name: Sarracenia 'Juthatip Soper'
plants.tip: Colour deepens through the season and peaks in autumn. Leave those pitchers standing until spring.
plants.colour: Tall pink-red pitchers with white windows and dark veins

plants.name: Sarracenia 'Adrian Slack'
plants.tip: Slow, costly and increased only by division. Give it the sunniest spot you have and never feed the compost.
plants.colour: Large white-topped pitchers with heavy crimson veining

plants.name: Sarracenia 'Dana's Delight'
plants.tip: The white shows best on late pitchers. Rainwater only, as tap minerals brown the lip within weeks.
plants.colour: White upper pitcher with fine purple veining over a green tube

plants.name: Sarracenia 'Scarlet Belle'
plants.tip: Sold everywhere in tiny pots. Move it to a deeper pot of peat and sand and stand that in a tray of rainwater.
plants.colour: Short broad pitchers, white-windowed with deep red veins

plants.name: Sarracenia 'Doodle Bug'
plants.tip: Stays low and small, so a shallow bog tray suits it. Keep it wetter than the tall hybrids.
plants.colour: Small semi-prostrate pitchers, red-veined with white flecks

plants.name: Sarracenia 'Leah Wilkerson'
plants.tip: It only reaches full size in a big pot in full sun. Divide in early spring, before the flowers open.
plants.colour: Very large white-topped pitchers with broad red veins

plants.name: Sarracenia 'Daniel Rudd'
plants.tip: Robust and quick to clump. Split it every second or third spring or it stops making full-size pitchers.
plants.colour: Stout pitchers with a white throat and heavy red netting

plants.name: Sarracenia 'Godzuki'
plants.tip: A compact hybrid for a small bog pot. It still wants full sun and three cold months each winter.
plants.colour: Small squat pitchers, green with red veining and a wide mouth

plants.name: Sarracenia 'Bug Bat'
plants.tip: The lid is held out over the mouth and keeps rain from the trap. Water the tray, never the pitcher itself.
plants.colour: Dark red pitchers with the lid held out over the mouth
